questions.question: On which peninsula did Rome develop?
choices: Iberian Peninsula
Balkan Peninsula
Italian Peninsula
Arabian Peninsula

questions.question: Which body played a major advisory and governing role in the Roman Republic?
choices: Senate
Estates-General
House of Commons
Council of Trent

questions.question: What name described Rome's hereditary aristocratic class?
choices: Plebeians
Patricians
Helots
Metics

questions.question: Which officials represented plebeian interests and could exercise a veto?
choices: Consuls
Censors
Provincial governors
Tribunes

questions.question: Against which power did Rome fight the Punic Wars?
choices: Carthage
Athens
Persia
Macedon

questions.question: Who became Rome's first emperor, receiving the title Augustus?
choices: Julius Caesar
Nero
Octavian
Constantine

questions.question: What does Pax Romana describe?
choices: The treaty that ended the first Punic War
A long period of relative stability within the Roman Empire
The complete absence of fighting anywhere in the empire
A law requiring all residents to become citizens

questions.question: Why did Romans publish the Twelve Tables?
choices: To establish the emperor's succession rules
To create a common currency for Europe
To abolish every social distinction
To make important legal rules available in written form

questions.question: How did Rome's Mediterranean expansion affect its economy?
choices: It brought new resources, trade, and enslaved labor
It ended contact with foreign markets
It restricted Rome to subsistence farming alone
It required abandoning all provincial taxation

questions.question: Why could army loyalty to commanders threaten the Republic?
choices: Soldiers had no connection to political conflicts
Commanders were prohibited from entering public life
Generals could use military support in struggles for political power
Military victories automatically dissolved the Senate

questions.question: How did Roman roads support imperial government?
choices: They replaced all maritime transport
They facilitated movement of troops, officials, and goods
They guaranteed equal wealth among provinces
They made local administration unnecessary

questions.question: What purpose did aqueducts serve?
choices: Fortifying ships for naval warfare
Recording laws on bronze tablets
Marking every provincial boundary
Carrying water to settlements

questions.question: How did Roman citizenship change as Rome expanded?
choices: It was gradually extended to more people within the empire
It remained permanently restricted to residents of one street
It was available only to people born outside Italy
It eliminated distinctions between free and enslaved people

questions.question: Why is Julius Caesar not usually described as the first Roman emperor?
choices: He ruled after the Western Empire ended
He was a Carthaginian rather than a Roman
His dictatorship preceded the imperial system associated with Augustus
He never held political authority in Rome

questions.question: What did the Edict of Milan in 313 CE provide?
choices: A requirement that every Roman become Christian
Religious toleration that included Christianity
The division of Rome into thirteen colonies
A ban on trade with the eastern provinces

questions.question: Which sequence is accurate for Roman political development?
choices: Augustus's rule, Republic, Caesar's dictatorship
Caesar's dictatorship, Augustus's rule, Republic
Republic, Augustus's rule, Caesar's dictatorship
Republic, Caesar's dictatorship, Augustus's rule

questions.question: Which comparison of republican and imperial Rome is best supported?
choices: Imperial rule concentrated authority while retaining some republican institutions
The empire immediately abolished every Roman office
The Republic had no political conflicts
Imperial Rome had universal adult voting

questions.question: A provincial inscription records a road built by imperial order. What relationship does it illustrate?
choices: The absence of government involvement in transport
The isolation of provinces from the capital
Infrastructure supporting administration and communication
The replacement of all taxes by voluntary donations

questions.question: Why is a single-cause explanation of the Western Empire's decline inadequate?
choices: Only one battle affected its history
Political, military, economic, and other pressures interacted
The Eastern Empire fell at exactly the same moment
No change occurred before 476 CE

questions.question: Which conclusion about Rome after 476 CE is accurate?
choices: Roman culture disappeared from every region immediately
Every Roman city was abandoned in the same year
Christianity ceased to exist in former Roman territories
The Eastern Roman Empire continued even after western imperial rule ended
